summary: A test-the-claim series. The hook (0 to 6.4-8.8 s) shows the claim under test in a rounded inset on the left (another creator's clip, or a repo page with a picture-in-picture), with tags stating the claim's surprising property, while the speaker stands to its right under a white 'Fact or Hype?' pill. A hard cut to a wider full-frame shot then lands 'IS IT FACT OR HYPE' in huge yellow italic on the chest. That shot lasts 1.97 s in all three reels. After it, a FACT / OR / HYPE checkbox bar sits across the chest to the end, and a panel fills the lower half: first the claim's own page (unframed), then a teal-framed screen recording of the speaker running the test. The body is jump-cut: 87-95 % of all detections are shot cuts, and the speaker's shot is cut about every 4-5 s (11-14 cuts/min in the body). Each jump cut also brings the next panel clip, so voice cuts and test steps move together. His own speech has no captions and the voice is cut tight (at most 2.7 pauses/min).

fit_notes: The format needs a real test with screen recordings. Without them, drop the panel and the bar; only the pill and the question shot transfer.
Reach the body rate (8-17 shot cuts/min) with take boundaries at sentence starts, each one starting the next test clip. Never cut words to hit it.
No captions on the speaker's voice in the source. For Thai or sound-off audiences, record whether captions.style 'mini' goes between the chin and the bar.
